title: How Precious Are Thy Thoughts of Peace
description: How Precious Are Thy Thoughts of Peace in Tonic Solfa to MELITA, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 110 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “God Good and Omniscient”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELITA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: How pre-cious are thy thoughts of peace, O God! to me, how great the sum! New ev-ery morn, they nev-er cease; They were, they are, and yet shall come, In num-ber and in com-pass more Than o-cean's sand, or o-cean's shore.

lines: How precious are thy thoughts of peace,
O God! to me, — how great the sum!
New every morn, they never cease;
They were, they are, and yet shall come,
In number and in compass more
Than ocean's sand, or ocean's shore.
Search me, O God! and know my heart,
Try me, my secret soul survey;
And warn thy servant to depart
From every false and evil way:
So shall thy truth my guidance be,

licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MELITA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
